budget.description: How many products OpenLinker reads from the shop in one run. Raise it and a full pass finishes sooner, but each run leans harder on the shop.

pageSize.description: How many products OpenLinker asks the shop for in one request. Asking for fewer means more requests for the same work; asking for more makes a single failed request cost more.

budget.description: How many products are checked in one run.

deletions.cadenceDescription: Together with the number above, this decides how long a deleted product can keep selling. It cannot be turned off.
deletions.intro: OpenLinker walks its own list of products and checks each one against the shop, so a deletion is found even when nothing told us about it. Some shops do tell us - a shop module can report a delete as it happens - and where they do, the audit is the backstop rather than the only route. This page cannot tell which is true for a given connection.
deletions.noSwitch: This page has no switch to turn the audit off, because it is what stops a deleted product's offers from selling. It can still be turned off in OpenLinker's server configuration, and this page cannot see that.
deletions.title: Deletion audit

operationalSettingsPage.description: How hard OpenLinker works your shop, and how long a full pass takes. Changing these trades shop load against how quickly OpenLinker notices a change.

hosting.catalogueSizeDescription: Used only to work out how long a full pass takes. This is what OpenLinker has copied over so far, which during a first sync is fewer than your shop holds.
hosting.processTimeLimitDescription: How long your host lets a single process run before killing it. Shared hosting is often 300 seconds. Ask your provider, or leave it at 300. OpenLinker cannot read it from your host.
hosting.title: Hosting limits

completed.ariaLabel: Days a completed sync job is kept
completed.description: How long a finished (succeeded) sync job's record is kept for troubleshooting, and to keep it from being re-run twice by accident. Bounded 30-365 days.
completed.label: Completed jobs kept for

failed.ariaLabel: Days a permanently-failed sync job is kept
failed.description: How long a job that ran out of retries is kept. It is the only record that the work was lost, so the default is longer than a completed job's. Bounded 30-365 days.
failed.label: Failed jobs kept for

caveats.notWhereItBreaks: Not where your shop breaks. These figures come from OpenLinker's own pacing, never from pushing a shop until it failed. They show load, they do not predict an outage.
caveats.oneService: One background service. If you run two, every request count here doubles.
caveats.sizeKnown: Pass lengths count the products OpenLinker has already copied over, not the products your shop holds. While a first sync is still running the real pass is longer, often far longer. The per-run figures are exact either way.
caveats.sizeUnknown: OpenLinker does not know yet how many products this shop holds, so pass lengths cannot be worked out. The per-run figures are still exact.
caveats.summary: What these numbers cannot tell you
caveats.testCatalogue: Measured on a test catalogue of 100 000 products, 3 variants each, 9 categories, no bundles. Your shop will differ.
